title: Proapoptotic RHG proteins and mitochondria are required for sensory dendrite pruning in Drosophila
abstractText: Abstract Caspases are best known for their role in apoptosis, but they are also deployed sub-lethally during development, where they contribute to cell fate specification, migration and terminal differentiation. How neurons activate executioner caspases without dying remains unresolved. At the onset of Drosophila metamorphosis, neighbouring sensory neurons in the dorsal body wall adopt opposite fates: class III dendritic arborization (da) neurons die by apoptosis, while the class IV da neuron ddaC prunes its larval dendrites before regrowing an adult-specific arborization. Their proximity allows lethal and non-lethal caspase signalling to be compared side by side in an intact animal. Using SR4VH, a sensitive dual-colour executioner caspase probe, we show that caspase substrates are cleaved in ddaC within 20 min of puparium formation, well before the proximal dendrites are severed, and at consistently lower levels than in its dying neighbours. Single-cell H99 mutant clones reveal that the proapoptotic RHG proteins are cell-autonomously required for pruning. Although reaper, hid and grim are all transcribed in ddaC as remodelling begins, mutant combinations suggest that reaper and grim, rather than hid, cooperate to drive branch severing and clearance. In addition, disrupting mitochondrial function or transport depletes dendritic mitochondria, prevents caspase activation, and blocks both pruning in ddaC and apoptosis in neighbouring class III neurons. Taken together, our data show that Reaper and Grim are required cell-autonomously for pruning, and that mitochondria are required for both caspase activation and branch severing.

title: Predicting different dimensions of fatigue from speech data: a longitudinal study in shift workers
abstractText: ABSTRACT Background Shift work, or working outside of normal circadian cycles, is associated with both experience of fatigue and poorer long-term physical and mental health. However, current methods for assessing fatigue present several barriers to building understanding of how these risks develop over time within individuals. Objective Here, we explore the potential of momentary speech activity-based fatigue measurement in a large, multi-lingual cohort of shift workers, using an intensive longitudinal study design (twice-daily measurement over two weeks in N =1,197 individuals from six different countries). Methods Paralinguistic speech features were used to predict different aspects of acute and chronic fatigue at each study time-point, with performance assessed in unseen (held-out) data. Results are reported both across the dataset as a whole, and for user-specific prediction models. Findings In the cross-sectional analysis, good (close to or exceeding current state-of-the-art) performance was achieved for both current sleep deprivation and self-reported sleepiness levels. The within-user analysis revealed robust increases in performance, yielding the ability to detect more subjective aspects of fatigue such as pervasive physical and mental exhaustion. Conclusions These findings offer preliminary support for the utility of using brief momentary speech samples as a low-burden, acceptable, and reliable measure of different aspects of fatigue in high-risk populations such as shift workers. Clinical Implications Developing brief, accessible measures of different dimensions of fatigue is an important step towards building understanding of how risks for poorer health outcomes develop over time within individuals exposed to significant circadian disruption. Summary What is already known on this topic Previous studies have indicated that speech data may be a promising source of information about fatigue: however to date these have primarily been carried out in small, unrepresentative samples and in non-naturalistic settings, making results hard to generalize. What this study adds Here, we present evidence from a large international study where participants both provided momentary speech activity data and reported levels of different aspects of fatigue, as they went about their usual working lives. Importantly, we use a modelling framework that explicitly takes into account potential influences of factors such as age, sex, and language on speech features and target fatigue measures, as well as assessing potential biases and reliability of model output. How this study might affect research, practice or policy If individuals who are at heightened risk of fatigue-related health problems are able to monitor their fatigue levels regularly and in real-time, this may yield the opportunity to intervene prior to transitioning into less tractable states of poor physical and mental health.

title: An Experimental Study on the Quantitative Mesoscopic Roughness Characteristics of Rock Using the Size Reduction Method
abstractText: Abstract The development of emerging clean energy technologies, including CO2 geological sequestration, enhanced geothermal systems (EGS), and underground hydrogen storage, faces a critical scientific and engineering challenge: the accurate characterization of complex fracture morphology in subsurface rock formations. Accurate quantification of fracture morphology is a fundamental prerequisite for engineering design and numerical simulation. However, current methodologies for fracture characterization often fail to effectively distinguish between detailed features such as fracture orientation and surface roughness, leading to imprecise characterization results that directly impact the quality of engineering implementation. This study introduces an innovative theoretical framework─the size reduction method─which isolates detailed roughness from surface tortuosity. Additionally, a novel detailed roughness index, Ra-r, is proposed to complement this method. Utilizing this advanced approach, the research conducts a comprehensive comparison of surface roughness across various fracture types: different regions within a single fracture, natural versus hydraulic fractures within the same specimen, fractures of identical lithology, and fractures of differing lithologies. The findings reveal several critical insights: First, within a single fracture, the roughness at turning positions is significantly lower than that in positions with a unidirectional trend, approximately 31.9% of the latter. Second, hydraulic fractures in carbonatite specimens exhibit higher roughness compared to natural fractures. Third, the presence of quartz mineral fillings reduces the roughness of carbonatite hydraulic fractures to 69.4%. Lastly, a comparison between carbonatite and shale fractures indicates that the roughness of shale hydraulic fractures is about 50.6% of that of carbonatite, while the roughness of natural fractures in shale is approximately 51.4% of that of carbonatite. This research offers significant contributions to the theoretical understanding and practical applications of fracture flow dynamics, providing a robust foundation for future studies and industrial implementations in the field of resource extraction.

title: A machine learning framework of ground-state properties of finite nuclei foraccelerated Bayesian exploration : NucleiML
abstractText: Abstract The global behavior of the nuclear equation of state (EoS) is commonly studied using data from finite nuclei (FN), heavy-ion collisions, and astrophysical observations of neutron stars (NS). The constraints derived from FN such as binding energies and charge radii play the most crucial role in shaping the EoS up to saturation density. The computational cost associated with explicitly incorporating these constraints presents a significant challenge especially when the aim is to explore the model uncertainties rather than optimizing a single model. We address this by introducing NucleiML (NML), a machine learning framework trained on ground-state properties of a few finite nuclei generated by a relativistic mean-field model. NML allows us to integrate FN and NS properties within a Bayesian inference framework in an efficient manner. The results demonstrate reasonable accuracy and a speedup of $\sim 10^4$ times for calculation of FN properties for a single parameter set, yielding roughly $\sim 10^3 \times$ speed up in the Bayesian framework. The present study makes the case for extending the work to a larger set of nuclei, potentially enabling future studies of NS properties to incorporate the whole nuclear chart.

title: Shotgun metagenomic characterization of human adenovirus F40 and a non-cpe Clostridium perfringens strain in pediatric prolonged diarrhea: a genome-resolved case study
abstractText: Abstract Background Viral–bacterial co-infections contribute to disease severity in pediatric acute gastroenteritis but are frequently underdiagnosed using routine methods. Enteric viruses, including human adenoviruses (HAdVs), may coexist with bacterial pathogens that influence intestinal pathology through virulence and antimicrobial resistance determinants. This study applied shotgun metagenomic sequencing to characterize concurrent viral and bacterial pathogens in a pediatric prolonged diarrhea. Methods Shotgun metagenomic sequencing was performed on a pediatric diarrheic stool sample, followed by quality filtering, de novo assembly, taxonomic classification, phylogenetic reconstruction, and integrated virulome-resistome profiling, including plasmid-associated resistance elements. Results Routine diagnostics identified adenovirus as the sole pathogen. Metagenomic analysis confirmed human adenovirus F40, showing close phylogenetic relatedness to globally distributed HAdV-F40 reference strains and a clear distinction from HAdV-F41. In addition, metagenomics uniquely detected a co-occurring Clostridium perfringens strain (SAM_A8, ST-5) that was not recovered by culture. The strain lacked the classical enterotoxin gene ( cpe ) but harbored a conserved histotoxic virulence profile, including plc , pfoA , colA , hyaluronidases, and sialidases. Plasmid-associated tetracycline resistance genes ( tetA(P) and tetB(P) ) were also identified. Conclusion Shotgun metagenomic sequencing enabled genomic characterization of a viral–bacterial co-infection missed by conventional diagnostics, highlighting its value for pathogen identification and resistance surveillance.

Thermodynamically Constrained Deep Learning for Hydrogen Sorption Prediction: Overcoming Classical Isotherm Generalization Failure through Physics-Informed Cross-Lithology Transferability
abstractText: Abstract Accurate prediction of hydrogen sorption in fine-grained geological materials is essential for subsurface energy systems. While classical isotherm models describe individual samples effectively, they fail to generalize across heterogeneous populations, with R2 dropping from 0.80–0.90 for single-sample fits to 0.09–0.38 for aggregated data sets. This limitation demonstrates that predictive models must explicitly account for intrinsic material properties and fundamental physical constraints. We present a thermodynamics-informed, physics-regularized neural network framework designed to improve predictive accuracy and cross-lithology generalization. The framework integrates three core components: a seven-category physics-informed feature engineering scheme generating 62 thermodynamically meaningful descriptors, a multiterm loss function enforcing saturation limits and monotonic pressure responses through penalty-weighted terms, and an architecture-diverse ten-member ensemble with post hoc temperature-scaling calibration to provide reliable uncertainty estimates. Van’t Hoff temperature dependence is incorporated through thermodynamic feature engineering, with all model components integrated within a three-phase curriculum training strategy that progressively introduces physical regularization. On a random-split holdout set, the framework achieves R2 = 0.9544, RMSE = 0.0484 mmol/g, and MAE = 0.0231 mmol/g, with a 98.6% monotonicity satisfaction rate and zero nonphysical negative predictions. Because random splits primarily evaluate interpolation within the observed distribution, we prioritize leave-one-lithology-out (LOLO) validation to assess physical generalization under distribution shift. When entire geological classes are withheld from training, the framework retains R2 = 0.723 for coal and 0.794 for shale, outperforming a well-tuned random forest baseline (R2 = 0.631 and 0.712, respectively) by 14.6% and 11.5%, respectively. These results support the effectiveness of thermodynamic constraints as a generalization scaffold across geological boundaries, providing a practical foundation for evaluating formations whose lithological classes are absent from the training data.

title: First Observation of D⁺ → a₀(980)ρ and D⁺ → a₀(980)⁺ f₀(500) in D⁺ → π⁺π⁺π⁻η and D⁺ → π⁺π⁰π⁰η Decays
abstractText: Abstract We perform the first amplitude analysis of the singly Cabibbo-suppressed decays D⁺ → π⁺π⁺⁽⁰⁾π⁻⁽⁰⁾η, using e⁺e⁻ collision data collected with the BESIII detector at a center-of-mass energy of 3.773 GeV, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 20.3 fb⁻¹. The absolute branching fractions of the D⁺ → π⁺π⁺π⁻η and D⁺ → π⁺π⁰π⁰η decays are measured to be (3.20 ± 0.06_stat. ± 0.03_syst.) × 10⁻³ and (2.43 ± 0.11_stat. ± 0.04_syst.) × 10⁻³, respectively. The decay process D⁺ → a₀(980)⁺f₀(500) is observed for the first time with an unexpectedly large branching fraction. Moreover, we observe the decays D⁺ → a₀(980)⁺⁽⁰⁾ρ(770)⁰⁽⁺⁾ and measure for the first time the ratio r₊/₀ ≡ ℬ(D⁺ → a₀(980)⁺ρ(770)⁰) / ℬ(D⁺ → a₀(980)⁰ρ(770)⁺) to be 0.55 ± 0.08_stat. ± 0.05_syst. These results offer novel insight into our understanding of the nature of the a₀(980) and f₀(500) states. title: 3C-guided reflection combined with scenario simulation for humanistic care education among nursing students: a mixed methods study
abstractText: Abstract Background Humanistic care is essential to nursing practice and directly influences patient outcomes. Since nursing students constitute the future clinical workforce, cultivating humanistic care competencies is an educational responsibility rather than a solely clinical issue. However, current training often faces challenges such as disconnection between theory and practice, highlighting the need for effective teaching models. Based on reflective practice theory, this study evaluates a multicomponent educational intervention integrating 3 C (Context, Content, Course) guided reflection with scenario simulation for humanistic care education among undergraduate nursing students. Methods A sequential explanatory mixed methods design was employed. In the first phase, all seven intact classes of first-year nursing students (total n = 350) from a medical university in Guizhou Province were included and randomly assigned using a random number table at the class level to either the intervention group (4 classes, n = 200) or the control group (3 classes, n = 150). The intervention group received a single, integrated 160-minute classroom-based session consisting of 40 min of theoretical instruction, 40 min of scenario simulation, 40 min of 3 C-guided reflection, and 40 min of summary and assessment activities, whereas the control group received traditional theoretical instruction within a 160-minute session that also included assessment activities. Outcomes were assessed using the Caring Ability Inventory, theoretical knowledge tests, and satisfaction questionnaires. Quantitative outcomes were analyzed using linear mixed-effects models accounting for class-level clustering; CAI models additionally adjusted for the corresponding baseline scores. In the second phase, 40 nursing students were purposively selected from the intervention group for semi-structured in-depth interviews, and data were analyzed thematically. Results The intervention group had a higher immediate post-intervention score on the self-report Caring Ability Inventory (CAI) than the control group (adjusted mean difference = 19.68 points, 95% CI 17.04–22.33; standardized effect size = 1.65; P < 0.001). Higher self-reported CAI scores were also observed for the Understanding, Courage, and Patience subscales. The intervention group also had a higher immediate post-intervention theoretical knowledge score (mean difference = 4.80 points, 95% CI 0.72–8.88, P = 0.021). Learner evaluations of the intervention were generally favorable. Qualitative analysis revealed four themes: empathy awakening, cognitive reconstruction through structured reflection, courage cultivation, and conceptual shift toward professional caring. Conclusion This sequential explanatory mixed methods study (a cluster randomized trial plus qualitative interviews) provides preliminary evidence that the multicomponent 3 C-guided scenario simulation model is associated with higher immediate post-intervention self-reported CAI scores and theoretical knowledge scores among undergraduate nursing students following a single-session intervention. Qualitative findings provided complementary insights into students’ experiences; however, the study design cannot establish long-term causality or sustained competency development. The independent contribution of 3C-guided reflection cannot be determined from this multicomponent intervention. The potential role of the “experience–reflection–abstraction” cycle warrants further investigation through multi-center, longitudinal studies incorporating objective behavioral assessments.

title: Towards Early and Accurate Disease Detection Through Multimodal Predictive Modeling: Fusion of Electronic Health Records, Medical Imaging, And Omics Data Using Interpretable Machine Learning.
abstractText: Early detection of disease is a cornerstone for improving patient outcomes, reducing costs, and enabling preventative interventions. Traditional predictive models often rely on a single type of data (e.g., imaging, clinical labs, or genomics). However, human health is inherently multimodal, involving a variety of data sources such as electronic health records (EHRs), medical imaging, wearable sensor data, genomics, and clinical notes. Integrating these heterogeneous modalities into unified predictive modelsoffers a path to richer, more accurate, and more robust disease detection. In this paper, we present a comprehensive survey of methods in multimodal predictive modeling for early disease detection, illustrate architectural patterns and fusion strategies, discuss challenges (e.g. missing modalities, interpretability, generalizability, bias), and highlight promising directions. We also propose a reference architecture for developing such systems and suggest evaluation best practices.

title: Long-term clinical outcomes of All-on-4 immediate implant rehabilitation: a 10-year retrospective study
abstractText: Abstract Background Immediate fixed full-arch rehabilitation using the All-on-4 concept is widely used for edentulous patients, but evidence integrating long-term implant, prosthetic, biological, and patient-reported outcomes beyond 5 years remains limited. This study evaluated long-term clinical outcomes of All-on-4 immediate rehabilitation over a maximum follow-up period of 10 years. Methods This single-center retrospective secondary analysis included 16 edentulous patients treated between September 2009 and September 2015, with 76 original implants supporting 19 full-arch fixed prostheses. Longitudinal assessments included marginal bone loss (MBL), modified plaque index (mPI), and modified sulcus bleeding index (mSBI). Three implants that failed during early healing were replaced and excluded from primary longitudinal analyses; sensitivity analyses were performed including replacement implants. Implant and prosthetic survival were evaluated using predefined criteria. Patient-reported outcomes, including Oral Health Impact Profile-14 (OHIP-14) and satisfaction, were assessed during postoperative follow-up. Results Three implants failed during early healing in one patient, resulting in an implant-level Kaplan–Meier survival estimate of 96.05% (95% CI, 88.26%–98.71%). All 19 treated arches remained functionally rehabilitated through the last follow-up or censoring. Two definitive prostheses required complete replacement because of ceramic chipping, and five screw-loosening episodes occurred in two patients. At 10 years, cumulative MBL was 1.79 ± 0.21 mm around vertical anterior implants and 1.85 ± 0.27 mm around tilted posterior implants, with no significant difference after adjustment. Both mPI and mSBI increased over time, indicating increased plaque accumulation and peri-implant soft-tissue inflammation during long-term maintenance, whereas implant configuration had no significant effect in the primary analyses. At 10 years, peri-implant mucositis was retrospectively classified in 37 of 57 assessed implants (64.9%) and 7 of 12 assessed patients (58.3%); no peri-implantitis was identified in available records. Conclusions Within the limitations of this small, selected, retrospective cohort, All-on-4 full-arch rehabilitation showed high long-term implant and prosthesis survival, with longitudinal marginal bone and peri-implant clinical outcomes documented over up to 10 years. Prosthetic maintenance and replacement were required during follow-up. At the patient-reported assessment, overall satisfaction with the treatment outcomes was favorable.

title: Integrated transcriptomic and metabolomic analyses reveal developmental and metabolic differences between wild and cultivated Cordyceps chanhua
abstractText: Abstract Cordyceps chanhua is an entomopathogenic fungus with both edible and medicinal value. However, the molecular differences between wild and cultivated C. chanhua during developmental differentiation and functional component accumulation remain poorly understood. In this study, transcriptome sequencing, untargeted metabolomics, and integrated transcriptome–metabolome analysis were used to compare cultivated fruiting bodies and mycelia (AF and AM) with wild fruiting bodies and mycelia (WF and WM), with a focus on gene expression, metabolic reprogramming, and bioactive nucleoside accumulation during the transition from mycelia to fruiting bodies. A total of 1,000 differentially expressed genes and 370 differentially accumulated metabolites were identified in AF vs AM, whereas 1,080 differentially expressed genes and 602 differentially accumulated metabolites were detected in WF vs WM, indicating extensive transcriptional and metabolic remodeling during developmental transition. In cultivated samples, the differential metabolites were mainly associated with amino acid metabolism, membrane lipid remodeling, and secondary metabolism. In contrast, those in wild samples were more closely related to glutathione metabolism, central carbon metabolism, and redox regulation. Integrated transcriptome–metabolome analysis further showed stronger correlations between differentially expressed genes and metabolites in cultivated samples, forming relatively compact functional modules. By contrast, wild samples exhibited a more dispersed gene–metabolite association pattern, suggesting distinct developmental and metabolic regulatory features under different growth environments. Functional component analysis showed that N 6 -(2-hydroxyethyl)adenosine (HEA) was significantly enriched in mycelia, whereas adenosine accumulated preferentially in cultivated fruiting bodies, indicating stage-dependent accumulation of bioactive nucleosides. Overall, this study reveals developmental differentiation, metabolic reprogramming, and bioactive nucleoside accumulation differences between wild and cultivated C. chanhua . These findings provide multi-omics evidence for understanding quality formation in C. chanhua , optimizing cultivation conditions, and developing high-quality functional food ingredients.

title: Temporal dynamics drive soil resistome variation more strongly than warming or biocide application
abstractText: Abstract Antibiotic resistance is a major global health concern. Understanding how climate change-related factors can influence antimicrobial resistance patterns in the environment is essential for developing efficient One Health-based resistance control strategies. In this study, under field conditions, we assessed the combined effects of soil warming and biocide (herbicide, fungicide, insecticide) application on soil physicochemical and microbial parameters, potato yield, and the soil resistome using the targeted metagenomics ResCap platform to quantify antimicrobial resistance genes (i.e., antibiotic resistance genes, metal resistance genes, biocide resistance genes, relaxase genes). To our knowledge, this is the first field study specifically designed to investigate the effects of the interaction between agricultural practices (i.e., biocide application) and soil temperature on the environmental resistome, thereby providing insight into the potential contribution of agroecosystems to the reported link between rising air temperatures and the increasing prevalence of antibiotic resistance. Our results indicate that neither soil warming nor biocide application were key factors affecting the observed variation in the abundance of resistance genes. Instead, the temporal dynamics during the growing season, as reflected by the observed differences between soil sampling times, was the variable with the strongest effect on soil resistome dynamics. These findings highlight the importance of studying the temporal dynamics during the growing season when evaluating how agricultural practices and climate change-related factors can influence the environmental resistome.

title: Development of a high-quality 90 K SNP array and its application in mining genes associated with wheat processing quality traits
abstractText: Abstract In this study, we report the development of a high-quality BAAFS Wheat 90K SNP array for the molecular characterization of wheat cultivars and systematically validated its efficacy in identifying genetic loci associated with wheat processing quality traits. This optimized array integrates high-quality SNP markers from the Illumina Wheat 90K iSelect SNP array and the Axiom® Wheat 660K SNP array, yielding a total of 84,661 loci. Among these loci, 79 are gene-specific functional markers and all loci are precisely anchored to the Chinese Spring (CS) telomere-to-telomere (T2T) reference genome, ensuring high genomic positional accuracy. The 84,661 loci are unevenly distributed across the A (37.9%), B (42.5%), and D (18.0%) subgenomes, with 46.91% of the loci localized within genic regions—an attribute that enhances the array’s utility for functional genetic analysis. Genotyping was performed on 190 wheat cultivars and 200 F 2 individuals derived from the cross between Shaanxibaimai and L43, generating high-quality genotypic data with marker call rates of 91.0% and 71.0%, respectively. A total of 1,041 Chinese wheat cultivars representing eight major agro-ecological zones were genotyped, and model-based clustering analysis resolved these cultivars into eight distinct subpopulations, with pairwise fixation index (Fst) values ranging from 0.265 to 0.503. Principal component analysis (PCA) showed that the first three principal components collectively explained 17.07% of the total genetic variance. Additionally, 2,478 recombination hotspots were identified, and these hotspots were predominantly concentrated near chromosomal termini. Genome-wide association studies (GWAS) were conducted by integrating phenotypic data of seven processing quality traits from Value for Cultivation and Use (VCU) trials, including dough stability time, dough development time, maximum resistance, extension area, grain texture, water absorption, and hardness index. A total of 294 significant marker-trait associations (MTAs) were detected, corresponding to 62 QTLs associated with these processing quality traits, and a pleiotropic region on chromosome 1D (408–423 Mb) was identified to regulate multiple dough-quality traits, explaining 7.18–31.56% of the phenotypic variance. Another key locus on chromosome 5D (2.7–7.0 Mb) was associated with grain hardness and texture, accounting for 0.11–16.53% of phenotypic variation. Novel QTLs, distinct from previously reported loci, were identified on chromosomes 3D (associated with dough development time and maximum resistance), 5A (associated with grain texture), and 6D (associated with water absorption). Candidate gene analysis was further performed for these three novel QTLs, and the pleiotropic QTL QDDT/DST/MR/EA.baaf-3D was found to explain 12.39–27.08% of the phenotypic variation for dough-related traits, highlighting its potential value for wheat quality improvement. To facilitate efficient marker-assisted selection (MAS) in wheat breeding, four Kompetitive Allele-Specific PCR (KASP) markers were successfully developed for key loci associated with processing quality traits. Collectively, the BAAFS Wheat 90K SNP array provides a cost-effective, high-fidelity genomic tool for wheat genetic research and breeding applications, including germplasm evaluation, genetic mapping, variety identification, precision breeding, MAS, and genomic selection (GS), with particular utility for dissecting the genetic basis of wheat processing quality and accelerating the genetic improvement of critical agronomic traits.

title: Analysis of risk factors for necrotizing enterocolitis in premature infants and clinical significance of serum SMOX and ACR
abstractText: Abstract Background: This study aimed to identify risk factors for NEC in preterm infants and evaluate the predictive utility of serum spermine oxidase (SMOX) and acrolein (ACR) levels for the early detection of NEC. Methods: A nested case–control study was conducted among preterm infants with a gestational age of <34 weeks who were admitted to the Neonatal Department of the Children’s Hospital of Soochow University within 24 hours after birth between October 2021 and October 2023. Thirty-two infants who subsequently developed NEC (Bell stage II or higher) were included in the NEC group, while 32 gestational age-matched preterm infants without NEC were randomly selected as controls. For each infant in the NEC group, one gestational age-matched control without NEC was selected using a 1:1 matching strategy, based on admission date, gestational age (±1 week), and birth weight (±200 g). Serum SMOX and ACR concentrations were measured on postnatal days 1,7, 14, and 28. Multivariable logistic regression analysis was performed to identify independent risk factors for NEC. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis was used to evaluate the predictive performance of SMOX and ACR. A combined prediction model incorporating clinical risk factors and serum biomarkers was subsequently established. Results: A total of 64 preterm infants were included, with a mean gestational age of 29.1 ± 2.0 weeks and a mean birth weight of 1223.0 ± 298.6 g. Compared with the control group, the NEC group had significantly higher rates of respiratory distress syndrome, sepsis, blood transfusion, and fluid overload during the first three postnatal days (all P < 0.05), and the proportion of infants who received early enteral feeding was significantly lower (P < 0.05). Serum SMOX concentrations on postnatal day 14 were higher in the NEC group than in the control group (249.2 ± 71.2 vs. 194.0 ± 52.9 U/mL, P < 0.05), whereas lower concentrations were observed on day 28 (213.2 ± 60.2 vs. 246.0 ± 63.9 U/mL, P < 0.05). Serum ACR concentrations were higher in the NEC group on both postnatal days 14 and 28 (66.1 ± 13.3 vs. 58.8 ± 12.7 pg/mL and 71.1 ± 15.8 vs. 58.7 ± 14.5 pg/mL, respectively; both P < 0.05). Multivariable logistic regression identified sepsis, fluid overload during the first three postnatal days, and elevated SMOX and ACR levels on postnatal day 14 as independent risk factors for NEC. A prediction model incorporating these variables yielded an area under the ROC curve (AUC) of 0.870 (95% CI: 0.780–0.960), with a sensitivity of 81.3% and a specificity of 90.3%. The Hosmer–Lemeshow goodness-of-fit test showed no evidence of poor calibration (P = 0.165). Internal validation using 1,000 bootstrap resamples yielded a 95% confidence interval of 0.787–0.961. The calibration curve showed agreement between predicted and observed probabilities of NEC. Conclusion: Sepsis and high fluid overload within three days after admission are independent risk factors for NEC in preterm infants <34 weeks of gestation. SMOX and ACR demonstrate good predictive value for NEC, and combined monitoring of these markers may improve the accuracy of NEC prediction and diagnosis.

title: Exogenous benzyl cyanide activates the somatic embryogenesis program in Arabidopsis
abstractText: Abstract Phenylacetic acid (PAA) is a naturally occurring auxin whose biosynthesis and function during plant regeneration remain poorly understood. PAA may be synthesized from phenylalanine via the CYP79A2-dependent phenylacetaldoxime pathway, in which benzyl cyanide/phenylacetonitrile (BnCN/PAN) is a potential intermediate and substrate for NITRILASE (NIT) enzymes. Here, we investigated whether BnCN/PAN promotes somatic embryogenesis (SE) through NIT-dependent PAA biosynthesis. Low concentrations of BnCN/PAN stimulated somatic embryo formation in Arabidopsis thaliana, whereas exogenous PAA also promoted embryogenic induction. Transcriptome profiling revealed that BnCN/PAN upregulated genes associated with SE, including key embryogenic regulators and EMBRYO DEFECTIVE genes. RNA-seq data further indicated enhanced auxin signalling, which was independently confirmed using the pDR5::GUS reporter line. Inhibition of NIT activity by heatin reduced the embryogenic competence of BnCN/PAN-treated explants, supporting the involvement of NIT enzymes in this response. Collectively, our findings provide the first evidence that BnCN/PAN promotes embryogenic transition and suggest that NIT functions in SE extend beyond their proposed role in indole-3-acetic acid biosynthesis. Summary statement This study uncovers a previously unrecognized pathway regulating plant regeneration, providing new insights into how naturally occurring metabolites influence embryo formation.

title: Synthesis and physicochemical characterization of ZnO-modified Fe₂O₃ nanoparticles with HCNFF-based prediction and AQAI-Net-based optimization for environmental applications
abstractText: Abstract Nanotechnology has paved the way for the development of Fe₂O₃ nanoparticles modified by ZnO showing high adsorption capacity and enhanced catalytic activity, which have gained great interest for advanced environmental remediation and photocatalytic treatment of wastewater. The use of intelligent computational tools in the synthesis of nanomaterials further extends pollutant degradation abilities, structural strength and environmental adaptability in varying operational conditions. However, prediction and optimization methods are existing and have poor prediction accuracy, high computational complexity, low convergence stability and low environmental adaptability. To overcome the above constraints, this research presented a Hierarchical Cognitive Neuro Forecasting Framework (HCNFF) and Adaptive Quantum Automation Intelligence Network (AQAI-Net) to realize intelligent prediction of nanoparticles and automatic optimization of the environment. The HCNFF predicted the photocatalytic degradation efficiency and adsorption performance with the hierarchical feature reconstruction and adaptive neural forecasting and cognitive learning mechanisms. Simultaneously, AQAI-Net implemented quantum-inspired optimization, adaptive learning and automatic control regulation for optimization of synthesis parameters. Experimental results showed that the system performance was better with a maximum prediction accuracy of 98.88% and optimization accuracy of 98.91% respectively. The general proposed framework was found to be very useful to propose a scalable and reliable solution for the sustainable environmental nanotechnology applications.

title: Adaptive Substructure Sampling for Molecules with Flexible Alkyl Substituents
abstractText: Abstract The exponential growth of conformational space in molecules with flexible side chains presents a fundamental bottleneck for atomistic sampling methods. A large fraction of this complexity arises from weakly coupled, quasi-degenerate torsional degrees of freedom that contribute little to chemically meaningful structural diversity while dramatically increasing computational cost. We present a substructure-based conformational sampling framework that separates flexible side chains from the molecular core at the graph level. Detached substituents are replaced by capped surrogate groups, enabling independent sampling of subsystems and systematic reconstruction of approximate full-molecule ensembles. A limiting variant neglects explicit sampling of the side chains and assumes extended reference conformations. This approximation is rationalized using high-level electronic-structure data for linear alkyl chains, which show that folded conformations become thermodynamically competitive only beyond well-defined lengths, particularly in solution. The approach is implemented within CREST and reduces the effective dimensionality of conformational sampling for molecules with extended flexible substituents.
venueName: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation

title: Continuous harvesting of intermittent and continuous heats by a mixed ion/electron thermoelectric generator using an ionogel blended with carbon nanotubes
abstractText: Abstract Ionic thermoelectric (TE) materials have drawn considerable interest because their thermopower can far exceed that of conventional electronic TE materials. They are typically implemented in ionic thermoelectric capacitors (ITECs) for heat harvesting. However, ITECs can harvest only intermittent heat, and there is no electricity generation under steady temperature. Here, we demonstrate a mixed ion/electron thermoelectric generator (MTEG) that can continuously harvest both intermittent and continuous heats into electricity. The active layer is an ionogel blended with single-walled carbon nanotubes (SWNTs), forming a mixed conductor in which the ionic liquid enables ion transport while the SWNT network provides electronically conductive pathways. Under a constant temperature gradient, the MTEG delivers a stable output voltage to an external load, closely resembling the behavior of conventional thermoelectric generators. The thermopower exceeds 11.3 mV·K − 1 , which is 1–2 orders of magnitude higher than the Seebeck coefficient of the best electronic TE materials. This operation is attributed to synergistic effects: hole tunneling across the SWNT network coupled with the large ionic thermopower arising from the Soret effect.

title: Trust in HPV vaccine effectiveness and safety and willingness to initiate HPV vaccination among unvaccinated female college students recruited through university-based online networks in China: a cross-sectional study
abstractText: Abstract Background Human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination is an important strategy for preventing cervical cancer and other HPV-related diseases. Vaccine trust may encompass distinct perceptions of effectiveness and safety. This study examined cross-sectional associations of trust in HPV vaccine effectiveness and safety with HPV vaccination willingness among unvaccinated female college students recruited through university-based online networks in China. Methods This cross-sectional online survey recruited female college students from 24 universities located in 12 provincial-level administrative regions of China between January 2025 and March 2026. The primary analysis included participants who reported no prior HPV vaccination. High willingness was defined as reporting being somewhat willing or very willing to receive HPV vaccination. Trust in HPV vaccine effectiveness, the safety of domestically produced bivalent HPV vaccines, and the safety of imported HPV vaccines were modeled as categorical variables. Multivariable logistic regression was used to estimate adjusted odds ratios (aORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Results Among 2,215 unvaccinated participants, 818 (36.9%) reported high HPV vaccination willingness. Higher categories of effectiveness trust and safety trust were associated with greater odds of reporting high willingness. Compared with participants who were very distrustful of HPV vaccine effectiveness, those who were very trustful had an aOR of 5.397 (95% CI 3.246–8.973). The corresponding aORs for being very trustful of the safety of domestically produced bivalent HPV vaccines and imported HPV vaccines were 3.307 (95% CI 1.930–5.665) and 5.022 (95% CI 2.741–9.201), respectively. Associations were directionally consistent after excluding participants reporting uncertain willingness. Conclusions Among unvaccinated female college students recruited through university-based online networks in 12 provinces in China, higher self-reported trust in HPV vaccine effectiveness and safety was associated with greater reported willingness to initiate HPV vaccination. Longitudinal and intervention studies are needed to examine whether approaches addressing effectiveness and safety concerns improve HPV vaccine uptake.

title: Stacked-Ring Aromaticity Rewires Quantum Interference and Through-Space Transport
abstractText: Abstract Stacking antiaromatic rings does more than switch aromaticity: it rewires how electrons interfere and flow through space. Here, we show that stacked-ring aromaticity (SRA), generated by cofacial coupling of 4nπ antiaromatic molecules, transforms their quantum-transport landscape. Vertical compression converts paratropic monomers into cylindrically delocalized aromatic dimers with continuous interlayer current-density flux and strong through-space electronic coupling. Remarkably, this antiaromatic-to-SRA transition systematically inverts the preferred electrode connectivity: the anchoring topology that favors transport in the monomer becomes the less efficient interlayer pathway in the dimeric configuration, while the alternative connectivity becomes dominant. This behavior arises from the reorganization of destructive quantum-interference features through interlayer orbital coupling. The effect is maximized near d = 2.70 Å, where magnetic reversal, energetic stabilization, and high interlayer transmission converge. This connectivity inversion is rationalized by a minimal Green’s function analysis as a layer-parity effect that changes the phase condition governing quantum interference in opposite-layer transport. Interestingly, the odd-layered stacking remains globally antiaromatic yet preserves efficient transport across the full three-layer stack, showing that the stacking-induced transport network survives the even–odd magnetic reversal. SRA therefore provides a mechanically accessible strategy for reshaping quantum interference and through-space conductance in molecular junctions.
venueName: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: COMPUTABLE ASPECTS OF THE LAVER PARTITION THEOREM
abstractText: The Laver Partition Theorem is a fundamental tool in the analysis of Laver and Hechler forcings. It is also connected to determinacy and the Galvin-Prikry theorem: indeed it can be seen as the common core of these two theorems. We study the reverse mathematics and Weihrauch degrees of the Laver Partition Theorem restricted to open and clopen sets. We obtain upper and lower bounds on the proof theoretic strength of this result, as well as a precise picture of the (arithmetical) Weihrauch degrees of the problems related to it.

title: The Off-Diagonal Low Rank Property: New Opportunities for Low-Scaling Computational Chemistry Methods
abstractText: Many matrices in computational chemistry are neither sparse nor low-rank, making the design of low-scaling algorithms difficult. In this Perspective, we point out that many important matrices in computational chemistry, such as the Coulomb matrix, the electronic repulsion integral tensor, the density matrix, the localized molecular orbital (LMO) coefficient matrix, the Fock matrix, and the nuclear Hessian matrix share the same property: when their basis functions are suitably ordered, their off-diagonal blocks have low numerical ranks (despite that they as a whole have high numerical ranks). This property, termed off-diagonal low rank (ODLR), has been extensively studied in the mathematics community, but has surprisingly found very little use in computational chemistry. This Perspective reviews the existing mathematical literature on how to use the ODLR property of matrices to compactly store, as well as efficiently calculate or use them. Subsequently, we review the use of the ODLR property in computational chemistry, and point out possible future opportunities of devising new low-scaling methods for dense, full-rank matrices, exploiting the ODLR property. In particular, we prove for the first time that Fock matrices and LMO coefficient matrices satisfy the ODLR property, even if the system is gapless (in which case the matrices are dense). This paves the way to linear scaling electronic structure calculations of gapless systems at zero electronic temperature.

title: Severe injuries in competitive cycling during an olympic cycle: injury patterns, time loss, and return-to-performance outcomes
abstractText: Abstract Background Cycling is an established Olympic sport associated with a distinct injury profile that has not yet been comprehensively investigated. This study aimed to retrospectively assess and analyze severe cycling-related injuries resulting in ≥ 3 weeks of time loss over a complete Olympic cycle. Methods A total of 192 cyclists were included, based on a retrospective online questionnaire assessing injury location, type, context, time loss, and return-to-sport outcomes. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, Chi-square tests, Mann–Whitney U tests, and exact tests (Fisher/Fisher–Freeman–Halton). Results Seventy-two of 192 athletes sustained at least one severe injury, corresponding to a 5-year period prevalence of 37.5%. A total of 237 injuries were recorded, with the upper extremity (33.8%) and lower extremity (27.8%) being the most frequently affected regions. Hand fractures (n = 14), clavicle fractures (n = 13), and non-specific knee injuries (n = 9) were the most common diagnoses. Significant discipline-specific differences were observed for hand fractures (p = 0.038) and shoulder dislocations (p = 0.046), while hand fractures also occurred more frequently in competitive athletes (p = 0.040). Clavicle fractures occurred predominantly during competition, whereas non-specific knee injuries were mainly training-related. Mean time loss ranged from 6.5 weeks for hand fractures to 13.3 weeks for shoulder dislocations. Return to pre-injury performance varied markedly, from 85.7% after hand fractures to 28.6% after acromioclavicular joint separations. Conclusion Severe cycling injuries follow two main patterns: competition-related traumatic injuries of the upper extremity and training-associated overuse injuries. Discipline-specific differences in hand and shoulder injuries highlight the need for targeted prevention strategies. The discrepancy between return to sport and full return to performance, particularly after acromioclavicular joint injuries, emphasizes the importance of sport-specific rehabilitation approaches.

title: Signatures of Novikov-Thorne accretion disks around rotating black holes in semiclassical gravity with trace anomaly
abstractText: Abstract Semiclassical gravity provides a promising framework to address the black hole singularity problem through quantum backreaction characterized by a coupling parameter, making it essential to thoroughly explore the accretion properties around such objects. In this paper, within the framework of semiclassical gravity with type-A trace anomaly, we investigate the thermal radiative signatures of Novikov-Thorne accretion disks around rotating black holes across diverse parameter spaces, focusing on the energy flux density, temperature profile, and thermal luminosity. Our findings demonstrate that the introduction of a positive coupling parameter suppresses disk emission, leading to lower peak values of both energy flux density and temperature, as well as lower peak values and corresponding peak frequencies in thermal luminosity compared to their Kerr counterparts in general relativity. In particular, this discrepancy becomes remarkably pronounced when the black hole possesses a high spin. Mechanistically, increasing the coupling parameter reinforces the effective gravitational field strength of the central compact object, which pushes the equatorial stable circular orbits outward and increases the specific energy of the orbiting matter, thereby reducing the radiative efficiency and weakening the overall disk emission. This suppression mechanism offers a potential astrophysical window to distinguish semiclassical gravity from general relativity and to place observational constraints on the coupling parameter via thermal disk spectra.

title: Survival of newborn and traditional practices of maternal and neonatal care- an analytical case-control study
abstractText: Abstract Background Pakistan has been reported to have the highest neonatal mortality rate of 39 (out of 1000 live births) among the South Asian countries. The disease burden in low- and middle-income nations is significantly influenced by financial restraints, delays in recognising danger signs, and socio-cultural factors. Most of these fatalities are avoidable. It is necessary to have a thorough understanding of cultural practices, beliefs, and family and societal norms to save precious lives. We have designed this study to determine the association between traditional practices of maternal and neonatal care and their effect on the survival of newborns. Methodology This is an analytical case-control study in which we utilise a non-probability consecutive sampling method. A total of 92 women (31 cases and 61 controls) who visited the outpatient departments of Paediatrics and Gynaecology/Obstetrics at Ziauddin Hospital, Kemari Campus, and lived in Gulshan-e Sikandarabad were chosen. The data were gathered through in-person interviews using a self-created, comprehensive, structured questionnaire with the assistance of community health workers. The data were collected from June 2021 to February 2022. The socio-demographics, maternal, neonatal, and neonatal care practices were the four main categories into which the variables under study were organized. The data was entered and analysed using IBM Statistical Package for Social Sciences version 20. Chi-square was used to compare appropriate practices between cases and controls. The odds ratios with a 95% interval were collected for all risk factors and effect modifiers by binary logistic regression. Multinomial logistic regression was used to determine the final predictors of the study. A p-value of ≤ 0.05 was considered statistically significant. Results On comparison of appropriate practices between cases and controls, significant associations were found between neonatal survival and the application of dressing on the umbilicus, time of first bath, cloth used for wrapping, exclusive breastfeeding, and getting the child vaccinated within the first week of life (p < 0.05). Multinomial logistic regression identified two factors of neonatal mortality. These factors were low birth weight (β 6.807,95% CI 1.77–26.10, p = 0.005), which increases the mortality ratio and vaccination of the child, which was found to have a protective effect (β 0.056,95%CI .011-.275, p < 0.0001). Conclusion Cultural practices were prevalent in the antenatal, natal, and post-natal periods, among which were found to be detrimental to neonatal survival. To achieve Sustainable Development Goal Target 3.2, it is high time to work at the grassroots level and create awareness for reducing newborn mortality by cutting down detrimental traditional practices.

title: Minor Structural Differences Tune Functional Specialization of Antenna Subunits in the PSII Energy Transfer Network
abstractText: Abstract Photosystem II (PSII) contains a diverse array of pigment–protein subunits with specialized roles in the antenna network. We investigate the functional significance of this subunit diversity in two structurally similar yet functionally distinct PSII subunits: minor light-harvesting complex CP29 and major light-harvesting complex LHCII. We combine two-dimensional electronic–vibrational spectroscopy with lifetime density analysis and structure-based kinetic modeling to assign spectral features to exciton states, providing molecular detail to probed spectral features. We show how the distinct pigment compositions of CP29 and Lhcb1, a monomeric subunit of the major LHCII trimer, reshape excitonic connectivity and energy transfer pathways in the complexes. Compared to Lhcb1, energy transfer pathways in CP29 are more spatially connected and reversible, suggesting that CP29 evolved to distribute excitation between the core and periphery of the PSII antenna. We find that small structural modifications from a common framework tune CP29 and Lhcb1 to complementary roles in the PSII supercomplex.

title: Quantum Sensing of Lithium Ions with Defect-Engineered Recognition Pockets in a TEMPO-Modified Covalent Organic Framework
abstractText: Abstract Nuclear-spin quantum sensing requires coherent molecular electron spin qubits embedded in analyte-recognizing local environments that bring target nuclei into their short-range hyperfine detection volume. Here, we introduce TA-TEMPO, a covalent organic framework in which dilute nitroxide radicals and Li+-binding triazine moieties form defect-engineered recognition pockets for room-temperature 7Li sensing. Optimizing radical density preserves spin coherence while maximizing the 7Li/1H response acquired by hyperfine spectroscopy. TA-TEMPO detects Li+ in a tetrahydrofuran solution of LiBr with a sensitivity of 1.0 × 10–4 mol·L–1 at room temperature, a 50-fold improvement over the previous benchmark, and enables quantum sensing across several lithium-based electrolytes. Control experiments and density functional theory calculations show that triazine sites preferentially bind Li+ over Na+ and position it near nitroxide radicals, accounting for selective detection in a large excess of Na+. These results establish chemically programmed host–guest recognition as a strategy to integrate sensitivity, selectivity, and coherent spin readout in porous molecular quantum sensors.

title: What works well for children and young people suffering acute pain attended by ambulance? A realist evaluation
abstractText: Abstract Introduction Access to adequate pain treatment is considered a fundamental human right, yet around 60% of children and young people (CYP) who need an ambulance for a painful condition experience poor pain management. We aimed to update our existing programme theory by exploring what works well for CYP, their parents/carers and ambulance clinicians. Methods We performed a realist evaluation using a multiple case study approach following the Realist And Meta-narrative Evidence Syntheses: Evolving Standards II guidance. We recruited CYP aged 4–17 years who had recently suffered acute pain requiring an ambulance, their parents/carers and ambulance clinicians. Study leaflets were handed out across three ambulance services and two children’s emergency departments in England from August 2024 to July 2025, alongside social media advertising. Participants shared their experience via face-to-face, online or telephone interviews, diaries, or through artwork. We also collected three years of routine clinical record data (January 2021 to December 2023) from two ambulance services in England. A realist logic of analysis was used to refine our previously developed programme theory. Results Twenty-one ambulance clinicians, fourteen parents/carers and nine CYP were recruited, producing forty-one interview transcripts, two pieces of artwork, and one diary. We also analysed 34,068 clinical records. Our refined programme theory identified the importance of ambulance clinician preparedness, particularly around education, training, exposure, and experience. The need for compassionate person-centred care was clear, particularly establishing privacy and providing reassurance, appearing calm, empowering CYP, allaying negative assumptions, using appropriate humour, building trust, and being aware of the consequences of unmanaged pain. The involvement of parents and carers was viewed as essential, with emphasis on alleviating their fear and anxiety. The programme theory also focused on the importance of pain assessment and treatment, particularly around covering visible signs of injury or illness, providing non-pharmacological distractions such as stickers, meeting expectations, and the impact of catastrophisation on pain assessment. Conclusion Insights from CYP, parents/carers, ambulance clinicians and clinical record data have enabled us to test and refine a programme theory for improving prehospital pain management in CYP. This theory can be tested empirically and used to inform future intervention development.

title: Cautious and risk-related behaviors among older pedestrians: the combined role of sidewalks, cycling infrastructure, and street trees
abstractText: Climate change requires rapid adoption of green street designs that encourage sustainable mobility, such as walking and cycling, while also helping to mitigate urban heat. In aging societies, these transformations must address the needs of older people. Focusing on Lisbon, Portugal, as a case study, this study explores how street configurations affect older pedestrians’ walking behaviors, focusing on environmental features and behavioral dynamics. Using a mixed-methods approach, we conducted structured observations of 911 older pedestrians and 1,340 cyclists in flow observations, and 174 older pedestrians in behavioral mapping, complemented by semi-structured interviews, across four streets with contrasting layouts (e.g., sidewalks and cycle lanes on the same level vs. separated, presence vs. absence of trees). Observations spanned four weeks in summer and fall, covering weekdays, weekends, and different times of day. Findings reveal that street design configurations are associated with cautious and risk-related walking behaviors. The study offers empirical insights into sustainable street design, supporting evidence-based policies to enhance older pedestrians’ mobility.

title: Penyebaran Informasi Film Animasi “K-pop Demon Hunters” Melalui Akun Tiktok @kpopdemonhuntersnetflix
abstractText: TikTok menjadi salah satu media sosial yang dimanfaatkan industri perfilman untuk menyebarkan informasi dan membangun keterlibatan khalayak melalui konten audiovisual. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis penyebaran informasi film animasi K-Pop Demon Hunters melalui akun TikTok @kpopdemonhuntersnetflix berdasarkan perspektif Teori Difusi Inovasi Everett M. Rogers. Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif dengan metode netnografi. Pengamatan dilakukan terhadap konten dan aktivitas pengguna pada akun tersebut selama Oktober 2025 hingga Januari 2026. Data dikumpulkan melalui observasi dan dokumentasi, kemudian dianalisis menggunakan model Miles, Huberman, dan Saldana yang mencakup reduksi data, penyajian data, serta penarikan kesimpulan dan verifikasi. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa penyebaran informasi dilakukan melalui konten audiovisual berupa potongan adegan film, pengenalan karakter, musik, dialog, dan penampilan pengisi suara. Keterlibatan pengguna terlihat melalui aktivitas like, komentar, share, dan repost, serta pembuatan konten kreatif yang berkaitan dengan film. Jumlah unggahan juga menunjukkan variasi, yaitu 13 konten pada Oktober 2025, 11 konten pada November 2025, 14 konten pada Desember 2025, dan 20 konten pada Januari 2026. Temuan tersebut mencerminkan empat unsur difusi inovasi, yaitu inovasi, saluran komunikasi, waktu, dan sistem sosial. Penyebaran informasi film berlangsung melalui strategi penyajian konten oleh akun resmi yang didukung partisipasi pengguna dalam menyebarluaskan dan mengembangkan informasi di ruang digital.

title: Patient-reported oral complaints during cancer treatment: Dietary consequences, supportive care, and self-management in a cross-sectional survey
abstractText: Abstract Background Oral complaints are common during cancer treatment and may interfere with eating and perceived quality of life. However, patient-reported evidence addressing dental and gingival complaints, xerostomia, taste alterations, counselling, and self-management remains limited. Methods We conducted an anonymous cross-sectional survey among adults in Germany with current or previous oncological treatment using paper-based and online questionnaires (January-June 2025). Analyses were based on valid responses for each item and included descriptive statistics, Pearson’s chi-square tests, linear-by-linear association tests, 95% confidence intervals for selected key prevalence estimates, and exploratory multivariable logistic regression sensitivity analyses adjusted for age and gender. Results The survey included 222 patients. New, additional, or worsening dental and gingival complaints during cancer treatment were reported by 41.9% (83/198; 95% CI 35.3–48.9%) of respondents. Xerostomia was reported by 56.6% (120/212; 95% CI 49.9–63.1%) and taste alterations by 68.0% (138/203; 95% CI 61.3–74.0%). Self-reported reduced food intake attributed to dental or gingival complaints was reported by 27.9% (57/204; 95% CI 22.2–34.5%), while 25.0% (46/184; 95% CI 19.3–31.7%) reported perceived quality-of-life impairment attributed to these complaints. In exploratory sensitivity analyses adjusted for age and gender, new, additional, or worsening complaints remained associated with reduced food intake (adjusted OR 7.85, 95% CI 3.70-16.62) and perceived quality-of-life impairment (adjusted OR 15.25, 95% CI 5.81–40.06). Among participants with xerostomia, the proportion reporting reduced food intake increased from 5.1% among those with no xerostomia-related eating difficulty to 91.7% among those with severe difficulty ( p < 0.001). Overall, 43.1% (87/202; 95% CI 36.4–50.0%) reported receiving support or counselling regarding oral health. Conclusions In this recruited sample, oral complaints during cancer treatment were common and were associated with eating-related burden and perceived quality-of-life impairment. These exploratory associations persisted after limited adjustment for age and gender but do not establish causality. Fewer than half of respondents reported receiving oral-health counselling, although perceived helpfulness was high among recipients, suggesting a potential gap in the reach of such support. These findings support prospective evaluation of repeated, function-oriented oral-health assessment and appropriate dental or nutritional referral rather than demonstrating the effectiveness of these approaches.

title: دور النشاط الرياضي المدرسي في معالجة ضعف الاستيعاب التطبيقي لمفاهيم الفيزياء لدى الطلبة في العراق
abstractText: هدفت الدراسة إلى تقصي دور نشاط رياضي مدرسي مصمم بصورة تطبيقية في معالجة ضعف الاستيعاب العملي لمفاهيم الفيزياء لدى الطلبة في العراق . اعتمد النشاط على مسار ركض مركب داخل مستطيل، تضمن مقاطع مستقيمة وقطرية ونقاطًا متعددة لتغيير الاتجاه، مع توزيع الطلبة على أدوار المتسابق، ومراقب الوقت، والمحلل، ومسؤول الحسابات، والمشجع. طُبقت الاستبانة القبلية قبل تنفيذ النشاط، ثم أُجري الإحماء قبل المحاولة الأولى، ونُفذت محاولتان يفصل بينهما وقت راحة، وبعد الركض شُرحت للطلبة معادلات السرعة والزخم وعلاقة تغير الاتجاه بالأداء، ثم طُبقت الاستبانة البعدية . شملت قاعدة البيانات 84 طالبًا وطالبة، وكانت 76 حالة مكتملة للمقارنة الكلية بين 12 فقرة متكافئة. أظهرت النتائج ارتفاع المتوسط الكلي من 46.93 في القياس القبلي إلى 49.83 في القياس البعدي، بفرق بلغ 2.89 درجة، وكان الفرق دالًا إحصائيًا (t = 3.887)،p< 0.001) )، مع حجم أثر صغير إلى متوسط (Cohen’s d = 0.446) ) ظهر أقوى تحسن في محور المفاهيم الفيزيائية (d = 0.558)، كما تحسن محور التعلم بالنشاط الرياضي (d = 0.402) لم تظهر فروق دالة في التحسن تبعًا لدور الطالب، ولم تظهر علاقة دالة بين سرعة المتسابق ومقدار تحسنه في الاستيعاب؛ مما يشير إلى أن القيمة التعليمية للنشاط لم تعتمد على التفوق البدني، بل على المشاركة والملاحظة والحساب والتحليل. انخفض متوسط السرعة من 4.720 م/ث في المحاولة الأولى إلى 4.535 م/ث في الثانية، ولا يُفسر ذلك بأثر الإحماء لأن الإحماء سبق المحاولة الأولى، وإنما بوصفه تغيرًا في الأداء بعد التكرار وفترة الراحة وربما التعب المتبقي أو استراتيجية التعامل مع الاستدارات . وتؤكد النتائج صلاحية دمج النشاط البدني مع تعليم الفيزياء في بناء تعلم خبراتي واستقصائي ذي معنى

title: KẾT QUẢ TIÊM TINH TRÙNG VÀO BÀO TƯƠNG NOÃN BẰNG TINH TRÙNG TRÍCH XUẤT TẠI BỆNH VIỆN ĐA KHOA HÀ NỘI
abstractText: Mục tiêu: Đánh giá kết quả phôi học và lâm sàng của phương pháp tiêm tinh trùng vào bào tương noãn (ICSI) bằng tinh trùng trích xuất tại Bệnh viện Đa khoa Hà Nội, cũng như các yếu tố ảnh hưởng đến kết quả. Phương pháp: Nghiên cứu mô tả hồi cứu trên 146 cặp vợ chồng vô sinh do vô tinh được tiêm tinh trùng vào bào tương noãn bằng tinh trùng trích xuất tại Bệnh viện Đa khoa Hà Nội, từ tháng 12/2023 đến tháng 11/2024. Trong đó, có 78 người được chọc hút mào tinh hoàn qua da (PESA) và 68 người được thực hiện vi phẫu lấy tinh trùng từ tinh hoàn (micro-TESE). Kết quả: Nghiên cứu cho thấy tỷ lệ thụ tinh là 72,59%, tỷ lệ tạo phôi phân cắt ngày 3 là 88,28%, tỷ lệ tạo phôi nang là 62,08%, tỷ lệ có thai lâm sàng là 77,4%, tỷ lệ thai sinh sống là 69,2%. title: Perilaku Kewirausahaan Dalam Memotivasi UMKM Kerajinan Di Kota Serang
abstractText: Usaha mikro, kecil, dan menengah (UMKM) memiliki peran penting dalam meningkatkan pertumbuhan ekonomi masyarakat, khususnya dalam menciptakan lapangan kerja dan meningkatkan kesejahteraan ekonomi keluarga. Salah satu sektor usaha yang memiliki potensi besar untuk berkembang adalah usaha kerajinan lokal yang berbasis budaya dan kreativitas masyarakat. Usaha kerajinan Karangantu di Serang Banten merupakan salah satu bentuk usaha masyarakat yang memiliki nilai ekonomi dan potensi pengembangan yang cukup besar. Namun demikian, pelaku usaha masih menghadapi berbagai kendala, terutama rendahnya pemahaman mengenai perilaku kewirausahaan dan rendahnya motivasi dalam mengembangkan usaha. Kegiatan Pengabdian kepada Masyarakat (PKM) ini bertujuan untuk meningkatkan pemahaman pelaku usaha mengenai perilaku kewirausahaan serta meningkatkan motivasi usaha agar mampu menjalankan usaha secara lebih produktif dan berkelanjutan. Program ini dilakukan melalui metode pelatihan, edukasi, diskusi interaktif, dan pendampingan sederhana kepada mitra usaha kerajinan Karangantu di Serang Banten. Materi yang diberikan berfokus pada konsep kewirausahaan, karakteristik wirausaha, pentingnya motivasi usaha, keberanian mengambil risiko, kreativitas dalam usaha, dan kemampuan melihat peluang usaha. Melalui kegiatan ini diharapkan mitra usaha mampu memahami pentingnya perilaku kewirausahaan dalam menjalankan usaha, meningkatkan semangat dan motivasi usaha, serta memiliki pola pikir yang lebih berkembang dalam menghadapi persaingan usaha. Program ini juga diharapkan mampu membantu pelaku usaha agar lebih percaya diri, lebih aktif dalam mengembangkan usaha, serta mampu meningkatkan keberlanjutan usaha kerajinan yang dijalankan. Program ini turut mendukung Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), khususnya tujuan nomor 1 tanpa kemiskinan, tujuan nomor 8 pekerjaan layak dan pertumbuhan ekonomi, serta tujuan nomor 9 industri, inovasi, dan infrastruktur.

title: PENGARUH KEMANDIRIAN BELAJAR DAN PEMANFAATAN MEDIA INTERAKTIF (CANVA DAN QUIZIZZ/KAHOOT) TERHADAP MOTIVASI DAN HASIL BELAJAR SISWA
abstractText: This study aims to analyze the effect of learning independence and the use of interactive media (a combination of Canva and Quizizz/Kahoot!) on students' learning motivation and learning outcomes in economics subjects. A causal-associative quantitative approach was employed, drawing from a population of 1,135 students at MAN 1 Lombok Timur. The sample comprised 296 students determined via the Yamane formula and proportional random sampling. Data were collected using Likert-scale questionnaires, computer-based multiple-choice tests, and institutional documentation, subsequently analyzed through linear regression assisted by SPSS version 27. The results demonstrated that learning independence and interactive media utilization positively and significantly affected students' learning motivation, accounting for 28.5% and 6.4% of the variance, respectively. Conversely, neither independent variable significantly influenced students' learning outcomes, each contributing a negligible 0.1% to the variance. These findings indicate that fostering independence and integrating interactive media are more potent in stimulating students' learning motivation than directly elevating cognitive achievement. Consequently, motivational enhancements via interactive media must be complemented by structured pedagogical interventions focused on deep conceptual mastery in economics. ABSTRAK Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis pengaruh kemandirian belajar dan pemanfaatan media interaktif (kombinasi Canva dan Quizizz/Kahoot!) terhadap motivasi belajar dan hasil belajar siswa pada mata pelajaran ekonomi. Pendekatan yang digunakan adalah kuantitatif asosiatif kausal dengan populasi sebanyak 1.135 siswa MAN 1 Lombok Timur. Sampel penelitian berjumlah 296 siswa yang ditentukan menggunakan rumus Yamane dan teknik proportional random sampling. Pengumpulan data dilakukan melalui kuesioner skala Likert, tes pilihan ganda berbasis computer-based test, serta dokumentasi akademik, yang kemudian dianalisis menggunakan regresi linear berbantuan program SPSS versi 27. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa kemandirian belajar dan pemanfaatan media interaktif berpengaruh positif dan signifikan terhadap motivasi belajar siswa dengan kontribusi masing-masing sebesar 28,5% dan 6,4%. Sebaliknya, kedua variabel bebas tersebut tidak berpengaruh signifikan terhadap hasil belajar siswa dengan sumbangan variansi yang sangat rendah (masing-masing sebesar 0,1%). Temuan ini mengindikasikan bahwa peningkatan kemandirian dan pemanfaatan media interaktif lebih efektif dalam menstimulasi dorongan motivasi belajar siswa dibandingkan peningkatan capaian kognitif hasil belajar secara langsung. Oleh karena itu, penguatan motivasi melalui media interaktif perlu diimbangi dengan intervensi pedagogis terstruktur yang berfokus pada pendalaman materi konseptual ekonomi.

abstractText: ABSTRACT Reading interest is an important aspect of elementary education because it encourages students to engage in reading activities and supports literacy development. However, limited variation in reading instruction may reduce students’ interest in reading, highlighting the need for more engaging and enjoyable instructional models. This study aimed to examine the effect of the Quantum Reading learning model on the reading interest of second-grade students at MIN 7 Bandar Lampung. This study employed a quantitative approach using a quasi-experimental method with a Posttest Only Control Group Design. The sample consisted of 56 students, comprising 28 students in the experimental group and 28 students in the control group. The experimental group received instruction using the Quantum Reading model, whereas the control group received regular instruction. Data on reading interest were collected using a questionnaire and analyzed through normality and homogeneity tests, followed by an Independent Samples t-Test using SPSS. The results showed that the experimental group obtained a mean reading interest score of 70.85, compared with 56.35 in the control group. The Independent Samples t-Test yielded a significance level of p < 0.001, indicating a statistically significant difference in reading interest between the two groups. Therefore, the Quantum Reading learning model demonstrated a significant effect on the reading interest of second-grade students at MIN 7 Bandar Lampung and may be considered an alternative instructional approach to support the development of reading interest in elementary schools. ABSTRAK Minat baca merupakan aspek penting dalam pembelajaran di sekolah dasar karena mendukung keterlibatan peserta didik dalam kegiatan membaca dan pengembangan kemampuan literasi. Namun, pembelajaran membaca yang kurang bervariasi dapat mengurangi ketertarikan peserta didik terhadap aktivitas membaca sehingga diperlukan model pembelajaran yang lebih menarik dan menyenangkan. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengetahui pengaruh model pembelajaran Quantum Reading terhadap minat baca peserta didik kelas II di MIN 7 Bandar Lampung. Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif dengan metode quasi-experimental dan desain Posttest Only Control Group Design. Sampel penelitian berjumlah 56 peserta didik, yang terdiri atas 28 peserta didik pada kelas eksperimen dan 28 peserta didik pada kelas kontrol. Kelas eksperimen memperoleh pembelajaran menggunakan model Quantum Reading, sedangkan kelas kontrol mengikuti pembelajaran seperti biasa. Data minat baca dikumpulkan melalui angket dan dianalisis menggunakan uji normalitas, uji homogenitas, serta Independent Samples t-Test dengan bantuan SPSS. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa rata-rata skor minat baca peserta didik pada kelas eksperimen mencapai 70,85, sedangkan kelas kontrol memperoleh rata-rata 56,35. Hasil uji Independent Samples t-Test menunjukkan nilai signifikansi p < 0,001, yang mengindikasikan adanya perbedaan rata-rata minat baca yang signifikan antara kedua kelompok. Dengan demikian, model pembelajaran Quantum Reading menunjukkan pengaruh yang signifikan terhadap minat baca peserta didik kelas II di MIN 7 Bandar Lampung dan dapat dipertimbangkan sebagai alternatif pembelajaran untuk mendukung pengembangan minat baca di sekolah dasar.

title: Engineering Synergistic Sites in a Cerium-Based Metal–Organic Framework for Photocatalytic CO2 Reduction
abstractText: Abstract Photoreduction of CO2 to produce solar fuels is an important target. Redox-active Ce-based metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) are promising catalysts. Herein, we have synthesized an amino-functionalized Ce-based MOF, PKU-167 (PKU = Peking University). Upon introduction of Co(bpy)2Cl2 (bpy = 2,2′-bipyridine) to the skeleton of PKU-167, PKU-167-0.9Co achieved a high CO production rate of 18.4 mmol g–1 h–1 with a selectivity of 91.8% under visible-light irradiation and an apparent quantum yield of 1.97% at 425 nm. In situ characterizations and modeling reveal a synergistic adsorption–reduction mechanism, where amino groups enrich adsorption of CO2 for subsequent photoreduction on {Ce6} clusters and Co2+ sites in concert to achieve the optimal photocatalytic performance. This study will advance the rational design of redox-active Ce-based MOFs as efficient photocatalysts.

title: Targeting the circ_0042819-PLA2G6 axis sensitizes multiple myeloma to proteasome inhibitors through ferroptosis induction
abstractText: Abstract Multiple myeloma (MM) is a refractory plasma cell neoplasm characterized by frequent development of drug resistance, leading to poor clinical outcomes. Activation of ferroptosis, an iron-dependent form of cell death driven by lipid peroxidation, has emerged as a promising cancer therapeutic strategy. In this study, we show that the circular RNA circ_0042819 exhibits high expression in both bone marrow and plasma samples from MM patients, with its overexpression strongly associated with disease progression and unfavorable prognosis. Mechanistically, circ_0042819 directly interacts with Up-frameshift protein 1 (UPF1) in MM cells, and the circ_0042819-UPF1 complex upregulates the expression of phospholipase A2 group VI (PLA2G6) via interacting with, and thus stabilizing, its mRNA. Furthermore, the circ_0042819-PLA2G6 axis suppresses ferroptosis through phospholipid remodeling in MM cells. Importantly, depletion of circ_0042819 or PLA2G6 enhances MM sensitivity to proteasome inhibitors (bortezomib and carfilzomib) by promoting ferroptosis both in vitro and in vivo. Collectively, our findings demonstrate that circ_0042819 is a potential non-invasive biomarker for the diagnosis and prognosis of MM, and that inhibition of the circ_0042819-PLA2G6 axis can mitigate the resistance of MM to proteasome inhibitors through ferroptosis sensitization, thus suggesting a novel therapeutic approach.

abstractText: Purpose This study examines how consumer food innovativeness and perceived food authenticity are associated with behavioral intentions toward fusion restaurants. Design/methodology/approach Data from 467 US consumers with recent fusion dining experience were analyzed using PLS-SEM and fsQCA. PLS-SEM tested mediation and moderation, while fsQCA identified configurations for high and low social media sharing intention and willingness to pay more. Findings Consumer food innovativeness and perceived food authenticity were positively associated with both intentions through self-congruity and emotional attachment, whereas attitude mediated only willingness to pay more. Moderation received partial support. Uncertainty avoidance strengthened the associations of food innovativeness with self-congruity and attachment, while attitudinal ambivalence strengthened the association between perceived food authenticity and attitude. fsQCA identified multiple configurations for high and low intentions. Research limitations/implications The findings extend self-congruity and uncertainty reduction perspectives by showing that consumer dispositions and offering evaluations operate through distinct psychological pathways and boundary conditions. Practical implications Managers can use these differences to guide segmentation, authenticity cues and communication strategies. Originality/value This study distinguishes consumer food innovativeness as a consumer-level disposition from perceived food authenticity as an offering-level evaluation and integrates net-effect and configurational explanations of fusion restaurant responses.
